newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's 96-97 coffee crop closes at 5.1 mln bags.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's 96-97 coffee crop closes at 5.1 mln bags.

text.p: Mexico's 96-97 coffee crop has ended down at 5.1 million 60-kg bags from 5.3 million bags in 95-96, the Mexican Coffee Council said on Thursday.

"The crop was slightly down," a spokesman for the government-backed umbrella group for the coffee sector told Reuters. Mexico's main harvest starts in October and lasts until March, although the high altitude harvest straggles on to June.

Exports to the end of the month of June from this Oct-Sept cycle had totaled 4.125 million bags (worth $798.4 million) compared to the 95-96 exports of 4.1 million bags to the same date (worth $595.5 million), he said.
Coffee receipts rose 34 percent on the back of buoyant international prices, he explained.
He said Mexican beans have so far been sold to more than 50 nations around the world, including the United States, Japan and and Europe.

Many coffee growers believe the pro-government council puts a political spin on its figures in a bid to show coffee as a dynamic exporting farm sector. Growers groups often estimate the national harvest at least 1 million bags below the official figure.
